title: fix(tools): holder form shows the outline's largest diameter; a covered body is not read back smaller
body:
## What changed

The cause of the mismatch is a label, not a wrong outline. A second defect under the safety floor was found during the work and is fixed here too. The MCP tool `edit_user_holder` (PR #4438, merged to `main` at `b6089ea6e`) gets the same fix.

1. **The label.** The holder form field `Largest diameter` held the body steel below the flange. For a BT40 ER32 that is the ER32 nut, Ø50. The drawing and the read-only view of a built-in holder show the largest diameter of the whole outline. For a BT40 ER32 that is the BT40 flange, Ø63. The outline was correct in the two views.
   - The editable field is now `Body diameter`.
   - A new read-only row `Largest diameter` shows the value of the drawing (`holder_drawing::largest_d`). This value is 2 x the largest radius of the outline.
2. **A body that the outline does not show (safety floor).** A shrink-fit body that the flange envelope covers shows nowhere in the outline. `HolderShape::of` then read back the narrowest body that draws the outline (the Ø38.748558 for a Ø44 body that PR #4438 saw). A copy of "BT40 Shrink 20 mm" read back a body of Ø41.544, not the table body Ø42. When the user then set a longer gauge length, Apply drew the body smaller than the steel.
   - `HolderShape::of` now returns `None` when a wider body or a narrower nose draws the same outline. The holder then opens in the generic component editor, as an outline from elsewhere does.
   - There is no exception for a copy of a library shrink chuck. A user holder with a wider hidden body can draw the same outline as a library chuck, and the component records no library source. A read-back of the library body would then be smaller than the steel of that holder. 44 of the 117 built-in shrink chucks have a covered body at their library gauge length (for example "BT40 Shrink 20 mm"). Their copies open in the generic component editor. The other 73 (for example "BT40 Shrink 25 mm") open in the form with the table values.
   - The new `HolderShape::component` builds the kind and the geometry. It refuses (`ShapeError::NotKept`, "give a longer gauge length") a shape whose outline does not read back as the same values. The form check and Apply use it. Thus the form never writes an outline that it cannot show again.
3. **`edit_user_holder` (MCP).** `crates/app/src/mcp/holder_shape_tools.rs` now builds through `HolderShape::component`, as the form does. It refuses `NotKept` with the same text as the form. It refuses a held holder with a covered body ("no holder shape outline"), and nothing changes. The test fixture moves from gauge 80 (a covered body) to gauge 120, where the Ø44 body shows. The shape edit goes to gauge 130 and body Ø46. The tool description and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` name the new refusal.

The decision record is in `docs/decisions/4455-holder-largest-diameter.md`. It records what was dropped: the library exception of the first form of this PR, and a "from the library" marker (a project file change, not done without the maintainer).

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-tools` lib: `holder_library::shape::tests::a_body_the_flange_envelope_covers_is_not_read_back_smaller`. It now also pins the look-alike: a BT40 bore 20 holder with a hidden Ø50 body draws the outline of "BT40 Shrink 20 mm", and neither outline reads back as Ø42.
- `camcraft-tools` lib: `holder_library::shape::tests::each_builtin_taper_holder_reads_back_as_its_shape`. Each built-in taper holder reads back with its exact table steel, or it is a shrink chuck whose body the envelope covers (a wider body draws the same outline). The write of the values read keeps the outline.
- `camcraft-tools` lib: `holder_library::shape::tests::an_edited_outline_is_never_smaller_than_the_steel` (each shape reads back exactly, or the write is refused).
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `egui_app::tests::tool_library_holder_largest::a_copied_holder_shows_the_largest_diameter_of_its_outline_and_applies_as_it_is`. It copies BT40 ER32, BT40 Weldon 12 mm and BT40 Shrink 25 mm. It checks that the form value equals 2 x the largest outline radius (63.00 for the BT40 ER32), and that Apply with no edit makes no undo step and keeps the geometry byte for byte. A copy of BT40 Shrink 20 mm opens in the generic editor.
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `egui_app::tests::tool_library_holder_form::*` (fixture at gauge 120, edit to gauge 130).
- `camcraft-app` `tool_library_holders`: `holder_shape_mcp::mcp_edit_user_holder_refuses_a_body_the_flange_envelope_covers` (new), `holder_shape_mcp::mcp_edits_a_user_holder_by_its_shape_in_one_undo_step`, `holder_shape_mcp::mcp_edit_user_holder_refuses_by_name_and_changes_nothing`.
- `camcraft-app` `mcp_doc_drift`: `the_committed_reference_matches_the_live_tool_table`.

`#[test]` count of `crates/ui`: 2009 before, 2010 after.

## Screenshots

A copy of the built-in "BT40 ER32", opened in the holder form. Before: the field "Largest diameter" reads 50.0, and the drawing shows Ø 63.00. After: "Body diameter" reads 50.0, and the read-only "Largest diameter" reads 63.00, the same value as the drawing.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4469/er32-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4469/er32-after.png) |

A copy of the built-in "BT40 Shrink 20 mm". Before: the form reads the body back as 41.544, smaller than the table body Ø42. The "after" image is from head `a16b70041`, where the library exception read the body as 42.0. On the final head the exception is removed, so this copy opens in the generic component editor (pinned by the UI test above). No new image was made for that.

| Before | After (head `a16b70041`, superseded) |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4469/shrink20-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4469/shrink20-after.png) |

## Gate

All steps ran on the final head `1e899ad44` in one `lanes` run (log `gate-4469-1e899ad44.log`). The branch has `origin/main` merged in (with PR #4438).

- `cargo xtask gate test holder_shape_mcp --crate camcraft-app --binary tool_library_holders`: 3 tests, pass.
- `cargo xtask gate test the_committed_reference_matches_the_live_tool_table --crate camcraft-app --binary mcp_doc_drift`: pass.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 182 steps, 0 failed. The MCP source change in `camcraft-app` puts each `camcraft-app` suite in the plan. The steps include `camcraft-tools` lib (the tools pinning tests), `camcraft-ui` lib (the UI pinning tests), `tool_library_holders` and `mcp_doc_drift`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- Targeted heavy step (P1, safety floor): `cargo xtask gate heavy --only "app heavy: tool_library_holders"`: pass. `cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run` shows the reach (the `app` and `motion` heavy lanes, from `camcraft-tools`). `tool_library_holders` is the binary that holds the holder tests. It has no `#[ignore]` test, so the step builds it in release and runs 0 ignored tests.
- The named `gate test` runs for `holder_library::shape` (tools) and `tool_library_holder` (ui) matched no function name. The quick gate ran those two lib suites in full.
- An earlier run on head `708582bbb` found two failures: `mcp_doc_drift` (the reference row was not written again) and `mcp_edits_a_user_holder_by_its_shape_in_one_undo_step` (a Ø48 body at gauge 130 covers the nose, so the tool refused it as `NotKept`). Commits `c7a6e5a84` and `1e899ad44` fix them: the reference row is written, and the edit states a Ø46 body.

## Not exercised

- A project file with a user holder that has a covered body (written before this fix) was not opened. Such a holder now opens in the generic component editor.
- No example catalog suite ran: the change does not touch a post or a toolpath generator.

Changelog: Holder form: the field for the body steel is now "Body diameter", and a read-only "Largest diameter" shows the same value as the drawing. A shrink-fit holder whose body the flange envelope covers no longer reads back with a body smaller than its steel: the form and the MCP tool `edit_user_holder` refuse it by name, or it opens in the component editor.

Effort: high

Fixes #4455
